_comment: History Toon — a subject in, a filmed documentary out. Pictures are real Wikipedia images resolved from the SCRIPT, so they follow what is actually said.
name: History Toon
description: Film a moment in history: a narrated documentary with real pictures from Wikipedia behind the cast.

config.userPrompt:
Write the screenplay for a short documentary film about the subject below.

WHO IS ON SCREEN. Three named people, all of them visible characters:
- CLARA is the historian. She carries the history: the dates, the numbers, the
  names, the causes. She is the only one who states a fact for the first time,
  and she speaks in complete, unhurried sentences.
- ADA asks the question a curious person would actually ask next, once.
- MILO draws out consequences — what it meant, who it was done to, what changed.

Do NOT write a character called NARRATOR, and do not write any voice that is
only heard. Every speaker is a person standing in the scene. A film whose facts
belong to an unseen voice loses them.

LENGTH. 700-850 words, which reads aloud in four to five minutes. CLARA should
have roughly half of the words. Give a speaker three or four sentences when the
point needs them; a script of one-line volleys reads as two people swapping
trivia, not as a film.

HOW IT MUST READ.
- Chronological. Say WHEN, in years, the first time each event appears.
- Explain causes before consequences. Someone who knew nothing should be able
  to say afterwards WHY each thing happened, not only that it did.
- Name people and places specifically, and say who they were.
- Plain declarative sentences. NO exclamation marks anywhere. None.
  Enthusiasm comes from what is being described, not from punctuation.
- No "Wow", "Amazing", "Incredible", "That's crazy", "Buckle up". No
  rhetorical questions.
- Every ADA or MILO line must move the history forward. Cut any line that only
  reacts to the previous one.
- End on what changed and what it led to, not on a summary of what was said.

ACCURACY. Only what the source material supports. No invented quotations from
real people. If something is disputed, say so rather than picking a side.

FORMAT. Plain text. One line per speaker turn, `SPEAKER: text`, speaker in
capitals. Nothing else — no headings, no stage directions, no markdown, no
preamble, no closing remark.

SUBJECT AND SOURCE MATERIAL:
{{INPUT}}

Below is a documentary screenplay. Choose SIX moments from it that deserve a
picture on screen, in the order the script reaches them.

For each, name the English Wikipedia article whose own lead image best shows
THAT moment. Rules that decide whether this works:
- Name the article for the SPECIFIC event, person, place, painting or object —
  never the broad subject. "Storming of the Bastille", not "French Revolution".
- The picture must belong to the period being described. An article whose lead
  image is a modern photograph is wrong for anything historical: prefer
  articles about a contemporary painting, engraving, portrait or document.
- Six DIFFERENT articles. Repeating one wastes a beat.
- Prefer a well-known article; an obscure person usually has no portrait, and
  a beat with no picture is a beat lost.

Return ONLY JSON, no prose and no fences:
{"beats":[{"caption":"three to six words","wikipedia_title":"Exact Article Title"}]}

SCREENPLAY:
{{INPUT}}
